name: LoFTR
plain: LoFTR (Zhejiang University, CVPR 2021): detector-free matching of two photos of one scene with transformers; semi-dense matches as keypoint pairs (the form COLMAP takes). Outdoor (MegaDepth) and indoor (ScanNet) weights. Apache-2.0 code and weights.
summary: LoFTR (Sun et al., CVPR 2021): detector-free dense matching. A ResNet-FPN gives 1/8 and 1/2 resolution features; a linear-attention transformer matches the 1/8 cells of both images (dual-softmax, mutual nearest neighbours above a confidence threshold) and a second transformer refines each match to sub-pixel precision in a 5 x 5 window at 1/2 resolution. Returns the matched points of both images, their (identity) index pairs and the coarse confidence.

papers.title: LoFTR: Detector-Free Local Feature Matching with Transformers

limitations: LoFTR Indoor FP32 ONNX Runtime matched all features within 0.00014 px on seven ScanNet pairs at 768 x 1024. Whole-graph TensorRT trials lost 5.27 AUC@20 points in FP16 and 2.58 AUC@10 points in FP32 on a separate 50-pair check.

The standalone ResNetFPN TensorRT plans took about 199 ms versus 273 ms for paired portable FP32 at 768 x 1024. The matching stages stayed in PyTorch. Each variant passed a 12-pair check that included its six worst whole-graph cases.
Sparse output: no dense warp. `result.matches()` gives the matched points for `estimate_pose`; every match is its own keypoint pair (`pairs` is `[[0, 0], [1, 1], ...]`).
One image pair per call internally (batches run pair by pair); the match counts differ per pair.
Match counts depend on image content. The verified ONNX export takes a fixed input size and returns variable-length matches.

Images are converted to grayscale and matched at `long_side` (default 840, upstream's MegaDepth test size); the coarse matching holds an (H W / 64)^2 score matrix, so memory grows with the 4th power of the side. The indoor weights were evaluated by upstream at 640 x 480 (ScanNet).
task_io: Input: two RGB images of one scene. Output: for every pixel of the first image its position in the second (x, y in pixels) and a certainty that the pixel is visible in both. Sparse matchers (LightGlue) return the keypoints of both images and the index pairs of the matched ones instead. To reconstruct camera poses from an image folder with these matchers, see [structure from motion](../sfm.md).

quality.protocol: Dense matchers: 5000 matches per pair sampled from the warp by certainty (upstream's balanced KDE sampling); sparse matchers: all their matches of one call (LightGlue, XFeat: LightGlue's MegaDepth-1500 setting; LoFTR, DeDoDe: their card defaults).
